title: Impact of air pollution on pulmonary function and respiratory symptoms in children. Longitudinal repeated-measures study.
ehr_evidence: Environmental monitoring network of Salamanca and direct clinical/demographic data collection via questionnaires and spirometry.
summary: Longitudinal repeated-measures study assessing the impact of ambient air pollution on pulmonary function and respiratory symptoms in school-age children in Salamanca, Mexico.
key_findings: Obstructive lung function abnormalities were more frequent in highly exposed students (10.4% vs. 5.3%; OR = 1.95, 95% CI 1.0-3.7).
A 10 μg/m3 increase in PM10 was associated with increased wheezing (OR = 1.0478), rhinorrhea (OR = 1.0318), ARTI (OR = 1.0977), and dyspnea (OR = 1.0184).
An IQR increase in PM10 (18.8 μg/m3) was associated with 3-month deficits in FEV1 of -0.37% in girls and -0.43% in boys.
No significant effects were observed for NO2 on respiratory symptoms.
captured_features: air pollutant levels (O3, SO2, NO, NO2, NOx, PM10)
data_source_type: Environmental monitoring and direct clinical/demographic data collection
population: 464 school-age children (6-14 years) from two public schools in Salamanca, Mexico
exposure_domain: Ambient air pollution (O3, SO2, NO, NO2, NOx, PM10)
limitations: Results cannot be generalized due to particular environmental and geographic features
Potential confounding from multi-collinearity among air pollution and weather variables
Unmeasured characteristics such as natural allergens, other pollutants, seasonal viral infections, and genetic predisposition
